en: to scrape up; to rake up

examples.en: I raked the scattered leaves on the ground into one spot.
I scraped together all the money I had and bought a present.
I gathered the trash in the yard and put it in a bag.

examples.ko: 흩어진 자료를 그러모으는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a day to gather up the scattered materials.

examples.ko: 용기를 그러모으고 나서야 대답할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Only after gathering my courage could I answer.
If we pull our strength together, we can win.

explain: 그냥 '모으다'와 달리 흩어진 것을 긁어서 한데 끌어모으는 동작의 느낌이 있어요. 낙엽 같은 물건뿐 아니라 '용기를 그러모으다', '힘을 그러모으다'처럼 있는 힘을 짜내는 비유로도 써요. '그러모아요', '그러모으니'처럼 'ㅡ'가 빠지는 활용이에요.

phrases.en: I gathered up my courage and confessed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨우 힘을 짜내어 한다는 비유로 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical figurative pairing for scraping up courage.

phrases.en: I filled the piggy bank with the coins I'd scraped together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 모은 것을 꾸며 주는 '-은' 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-은' modifier form describing things already gathered.

phrases.en: I'm gathering up the toys scattered on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하고 있는 동작을 말하는 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The progressive form for an action happening now.

explain_en: Unlike plain '모으다', it has the feel of scraping scattered things together. Besides objects like leaves, it is used figuratively for summoning what you have, as in '용기를 그러모으다' or '힘을 그러모으다'. The ㅡ drops in conjugation: '그러모아요', '그러모으니'.

en: to be urgent; to be pressing

examples.en: The situation is urgent, so there's no time to explain.

examples.ko: 급박한 소식을 듣고 바로 병원으로 달려갔어요.
examples.en: I heard the urgent news and ran straight to the hospital.

examples.ko: 마감이 급박하니까 오늘 밤을 새워야 해요.
examples.en: The deadline is pressing, so I have to stay up all night.
Her voice on the phone sounded urgent, so I was worried.

examples.ko: 그렇게 급박하지 않으면 내일 얘기해도 돼요.
examples.en: If it's not that urgent, we can talk about it tomorrow.

examples.ko: 사고 직전의 급박했던 순간이 아직도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the tense, urgent moment right before the accident.

explain: '급하다'는 마음이나 일 전반에 쓰지만, '급박하다'는 상황이나 사정이 몰려서 당장 움직여야 할 때 써요. 성격이 급한 사람에게는 '급하다'를 쓰고, '급박한 상황'처럼 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: It was an urgent situation, so I had to decide right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 당장 움직여야 하는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for moments that demand immediate action.

phrases.en: Things at the company are moving at a pressing pace these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 몰려서 빠르게 진행될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when events are piling up and moving fast.
phrases.en_equiv: to move at a pressing pace

phrases.en: The final scene of the movie was really tense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 긴장감이 더 강하게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but with a stronger sense of tension.

explain_en: '급하다' can describe feelings or tasks in general, but '급박하다' is for a situation that is closing in so you must act right now. For an impatient person you use '급하다'. It appears more in news and writing, as in '급박한 상황'.

examples.en: Don't hang around out late; come home early.
I don't like going out and about on rainy days.
These days my younger sibling goes out with friends every day.

examples.ko: 아픈 사람이 여기저기 나다니면 안 돼요.
examples.en: A sick person shouldn't be going around everywhere.
I don't know where on earth he goes every weekend.
As a kid, I played while roaming around the neighborhood.

explain: 특별한 볼일 없이 자꾸 밖에 나가 돌아다닌다는 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 부모님이 "밤에 나다니지 마"라고 하듯이 걱정이나 잔소리에 잘 나와요. 단순히 이동하는 '돌아다니다'보다 못마땅한 뉘앙스가 강해요. 문장 끝의 '-다니'(예: 일어나다니)와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: It's dangerous at night, so don't wander around.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, worried warning to family or friends.

phrases.en: My younger sibling keeps going out at night these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 나타내는 말과 함께 쓰면 못마땅한 느낌이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: With a time word, the disapproving tone comes through more clearly.

phrases.example: 그는 집에 있지 않고 나다니는 버릇이 있어요.
phrases.en: He has a habit of going out instead of staying home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 돌아다니는 습관을 못마땅하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a habit of roaming around with some disapproval.

explain_en: It carries a slightly negative feel of going out and about again and again without any real errand. It often appears in worry or nagging, like a parent saying '밤에 나다니지 마' (don't roam around at night). It is more disapproving than the neutral '돌아다니다'. It is unrelated to the '-다니' ending, as in '일어나다니'.

examples.ko: 도주 중인 범인을 경찰이 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are looking for the criminal on the run.
We confirmed the escape route on CCTV.
He did not succeed in escaping in the end.
He was detained because he was a flight risk.

examples.ko: 영화 속 도주 장면이 정말 아슬아슬했어요.
examples.en: The escape scene in the movie was really thrilling.
The person who helped with the escape was caught too.

explain: 도주는 범죄와 관련된 뉴스에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 일상에서 도망가는 것은 '도망'이 더 흔하고, 가볍게는 '튀다'라고도 해요. '도주 차량', '도주 우려'가 자주 보이는 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The criminal fled in a car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도주'를 동사로 쓴 말로, 뉴스에서 범인이 달아났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 도주, used in news when a criminal runs away.

phrases.example: 도주 우려가 있어서 경찰이 용의자를 체포했어요.
phrases.en: Because there was a risk of flight, the police arrested the suspect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법이나 뉴스에서 달아날 가능성이 있다는 뜻으로 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in law and news meaning there is a chance the person will run away.

phrases.en: The puppy ran away while the door was open.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도주'보다 일상적이고 범죄와 상관없는 상황에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 도주 and can be used in situations unrelated to crime.

explain_en: This word is common in crime news. In everyday talk, '도망' is more usual for running away, and the slangy '튀다' is also used. Frequent pairings are '도주 차량' (getaway vehicle) and '도주 우려' (flight risk).

examples.en: The baby is laughing, kicking its legs about.
The caught fish is thrashing around in my hand.

examples.ko: 아이가 안아 달라고 버둥버둥 몸을 비틀어요.
examples.en: The child twists and squirms, asking to be picked up.

examples.ko: 바닥에 뒤집힌 거북이가 버둥버둥 애쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: The turtle flipped over on the floor is struggling hard.

examples.ko: 고양이가 목욕이 싫어서 버둥버둥 난리를 쳐요.
examples.en: The cat hates baths and makes a big fuss, thrashing about.

examples.ko: 버둥버둥 애를 써 봐도 일이 풀리지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I struggle, things don't work out.

explain: 팔다리를 크게 흔들며 움직이는 모양이에요. '바둥바둥'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요. 어려운 일 앞에서 애쓰는 모습을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The baby struggles because it doesn't want to be held.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버둥버둥'과 같은 뜻의 동사예요. 동작을 바로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb with the same meaning as 버둥버둥, used to describe the action directly.

phrases.en: I'm struggling hard to pay off my debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 일 앞에서 힘들게 노력하는 모습을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for working hard against a difficulty.

phrases.en: The person who fell into the water thrashes about.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔다리를 흔드는 동작과 필사적으로 애쓰는 것을 모두 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can mean thrashing one's limbs or trying desperately.

explain_en: It shows the motion of waving arms and legs about widely. '바둥바둥' feels smaller and lighter. It can also describe struggling hard against a difficult situation.

examples.en: We have to clear the snow in the yard with a shovel.
Once I cut off the branches, the yard became bright.

examples.ko: 하수구에 쌓인 흙을 쳐내서 물이 잘 빠져요.
examples.en: I cleared out the dirt piled up in the drain, so water drains well now.
The goalkeeper batted away the incoming ball with his hand.

examples.ko: 회사가 비용이 많이 드는 부서를 쳐내기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to cut away the departments that cost a lot.

examples.ko: 연못 바닥의 낙엽을 쳐내는 일을 도왔어요.
examples.en: I helped with clearing out the fallen leaves from the bottom of the pond.

explain: 쌓인 것(눈, 흙)을 퍼서 없애거나, 나뭇가지처럼 필요 없는 부분을 잘라 낼 때 써요. 공을 쳐서 밖으로 보내는 뜻도 있어요. '치우다'보다 힘을 들여 덜어 낸다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I scooped the soil out of the ditch with a shovel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓인 흙을 퍼서 덜어 낼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when scooping out piled-up soil.

phrases.example: 필요 없는 가지는 다 쳐내 버렸어요.
phrases.en: I cut off all the unneeded branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 버리다'를 붙이면 완전히 없앴다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 버리다 strengthens the feeling of getting rid of it completely.

phrases.en: The defender knocked the incoming ball far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공을 쳐서 밖으로 보낸다는 다른 뜻으로 운동 경기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The other meaning, hitting a ball away, used in sports.

explain_en: It is used for scooping away piled-up things like snow or dirt, or cutting off unneeded parts like branches. It can also mean hitting a ball away. Compared with '치우다', it feels like removing something with some effort.
